title: For the Rough Sleeping Outreach and Navigator Procurement
description: RSI services aim to prevent rough sleeping where possible and where not possible to ensure it is rare, brief and non-recurring. RSI Outreach workers take the lead in identifying and engaging individuals who are rough sleeping across the borough and supporting them into suitable accommodation pathways. The RSI Navigator support is key to tenancy sustainment for a cohort of identified entrenched rough sleepers. Commission an RSI Navigator service using grant monies awarded to the council. The most recent grant award of RSI Navigator funding is made by GMCA and runs from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2029. The RSI Navigator service ensures that we are working towards ending rough sleeping within the borough and is based on assisting with the delivery of the three principles identified in the Oldham Rough Sleeping Plan; 1. Prevention - Stopping people sleeping rough for the first time. 2. Intervention - Support to those currently sleeping rough to move off the streets. 3. Recovery - Support to those who have slept rough to ensure they don't return to the streets The appointed RSI Navigator provider is tasked with sourcing accommodation and building effective networks of support for rough sleepers in the borough. The RSI Navigator provider is key to tenancy sustainment for the cohort of identified entrenched rough sleepers. The ongoing support provided by the RSI Navigator provider continues with service users through their journey in temporary accommodation schemes such as A Bed Every Night (ABEN) and stays with them when they are housed in an independent tenancy, in either the social or private sector.

Hankinta sisältää tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmien ja niiden hallinta-alustan toimittamisen ja käyttöönoton käyttökuntoon saakka, sekä korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalvelut. Hankinta sisältää seuraavat järjestelmätoimitukset: - Kulunvalvontajärjestelmä - Kameravalvontajärjestelmä - Rikosilmoitinjärjestelmä - Ovipuhelinjärjestelmä - Henkilöturvajärjestelmä - Hätäkuulutusjärjestelmä - Lukitusjärjestelmä - VIRVE-verkko - Järjestelmäkokonaisuuden hallinta-alusta Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus tulee sijoittumaan Tikkurilan osaamiskampuksen alueelle lähelle Tikkurilan asemaa, osoitteeseen Jokiniemenkatu 1, 01370 Vantaa. Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus käsittää opiskelutilat noin 2600 opiskelijalle viidestä eri oppilaitoksesta: Vantaan Ammattiopisto Variasta, Tikkurilan lukiosta, Tikkurilan iltalukiosta, Vantaan aikuisopistosta ja Vantaan Musiikkiopistosta. Lisäksi henkilökuntaa on noin 300. Oppilaitoskorttelissa on kellarikerroksen lisäksi maan päällä kuusi opetustoiminnan kerrosta ja IV-konehuonekerros. Hankesuunnitelman mukainen laajuus on 25 200 brm2 ja tontin pinta-ala on noin 7900 m2. Kohde on toiminnaltaan, sijainniltaan ja turvallisuusympäristöltään poikkeuksellisen vaativa. Kohteen tilaturvallisuudessa on huomioitava useat käyttäjäryhmät, jotka käyttävät kiinteistöä eri tavoin ja eri ajankohtina, sekä laaja määrä julkisia tiloja, joihin on kulku pääsisäänkäynnin kautta. Lisäksi järjestelmätoimituksissa on huomioitava tilojen muuntojoustavuus sekä toimitettavien järjestelmien skaalautuvuus tulevaisuudessa myös muihin kiinteistöihin ja uusille käyttäjäryhmille. Hankittavaan urakkaan kuuluu 24 kuukauden takuuaika ja pidennetyt takuuajat. Työssä noudatetaan urakkatoimituksen osalta YSE 1998 -ehtoja, sekä palveluiden osalta JYSE-palvelut 2025 -ehtoja tarjouspyynnössä ja sopimuksessa esitetyin poikkeuksin. Oppilaitoskortteli -uudisrakennus käsittää opiskelutilat noin 2600 opiskelijalle viidestä eri oppilaitoksesta: Vantaan Ammattiopisto Variasta, Tikkurilan lukiosta, Tikkurilan iltalukiosta, Vantaan aikuisopistosta ja Vantaan Musiikkiopistosta. Lisäksi henkilökuntaa on noin 300. Oppilaitoskorttelissa on kellarikerroksen lisäksi maan päällä kuusi opetustoiminnan kerrosta ja IV-konehuonekerros. Hankesuunnitelman mukainen laajuus on 25 200 brm2 ja tontin pinta-ala on noin 7900 m2. Kohde on toiminnaltaan, sijainniltaan ja turvallisuusympäristöltään poikkeuksellisen vaativa. Hankittavaan urakkaan kuuluu 24 kuukauden takuuaika ja pidennetyt takuuajat. Työssä noudatetaan urakkatoimituksen osalta YSE 1998 -ehtoja, sekä palveluiden osalta JYSE-palvelut 2025 -ehtoja tarjouspyynnössä ja sopimuksessa esitetyin poikkeuksin. title: Social and emotional robot
description: Social and emotional robot The procurement consists of one (1) programmable and interactive social and emotional humanoid/service robot. The total value of the procurement shall not exceed EUR 75,000 (VAT 0%). The robot shall be designed for safe indoor operation and human interaction. It must support Finnish-language communication and be capable of facilitating social interaction, autonomous activities, emotional engagement, and the safe handling of objects. The robot must be suitable for educational, guidance, rehabilitation, and student support environments. The primary purpose of the procurement is to support Care Assistant Education by providing students with hands-on experience in healthcare and welfare technologies, social robotics, communication, guidance, and technology-assisted care. The robot will also be used in simulation-based learning and to familiarise students with technologies commonly encountered in modern working life. In addition, the robot will be available for multidisciplinary use across the contracting authority's educational programmes and support services. It will function as a shared pedagogical resource that promotes communication, participation, digital skills, and familiarity with emerging technologies. The robot may be used in various educational and operational roles, including learning support, interactive communication, visitor guidance, information sharing, wellbeing reminders, event reception, and customer interaction training. The contracting authority seeks a versatile, user-friendly, and pedagogically effective solution that supports inclusive learning environments and provides long-term value across multiple user groups and educational contexts.,

description: Amendment # 001 raised to amend the solicitation closing date and answer questions from industry. Amended the UNSPSC of the Tender Notice. Offers. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a Technical Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis on Fuel Storage Tank Systems Life Cycle (Installation, Maintenance and Removal) to Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) as described in Annex Statement of Work. The technical assessment and cost-benefit analysis will evaluate various options for the installation, maintenance, and decommissioning of storage tank systems and how they align with current industry practices in Canada. The analysis must identify associated environmental impacts, resource requirements, benefits, challenges, and operational and policy risks such as regulatory misalignment, compliance barriers, or unintended socioeconomic consequences that go beyond environmental considerations. This includes considerations for both the regulated community and key industry stakeholders such as certified installers, professional engineers, project managers, consultants, and manufacturers. The Contractor must assess the most common and practical procedures currently used in the industry for the installation, maintenance, including leak detection options, and decommissioning of various types of storage tank systems located in Canada. The Contractor must review applicable requirements under the National Fire Code of Canada (NFCC), CSA B139 Installation Code for Oil-Burning Equipment, the CCME Code of Practice, and any other authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) with best requirements for protecting against fuel contamination. Term. The period of the Contract is from date of Contract (est. October 1, 2026) to December 31, 2027, inclusive. Resource Categories The resource categories (roles)* required are as follows: 1. Licensed Professional Engineer 2. Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician 3. Petroleum Storage Tank Systems Compliance Specialist 4. Project Manager *As part of its proposed Project Team, the Offeror can propose the same resource for any of the resource categories required, with the exception that the Licensed Professional Engineer cannot be the same proposed resource as the Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician. Note to Offerors: The proposed resource title (resource categories) in Annex Technical Criteria are descriptive labels intended solely to indicate the nature of the expertise required. They do not represent formal occupational classifications or restrict the number of resources proposed, the allocation of responsibilities, or the manner in which an Offeror structures its Project Team.

For table one Table 1 – All level of efforts (labour) and mandatory replacement parts to bring the MP Police vehicles and related items in accordance with Annex - Statement of Work (SOW). The SOW clearly indicates what must be installed. Other than Decals it does not clearly identify if the equipment is all net new, mix between new and reconditioned, or all reconditioned. What equipment is new or not? Answer 5. All equipment must be new ________________________________________ Question 6. Is Table 1 to be priced based on labour, shop supplies, and decals only? Answer 6. Yes ________________________________________ Question 7. That all decommissioned equipment is to be reused providing it is operational as intended? That net new equipment will fall under Table 5. Answer 7. No equipment can be reused, must be new. ________________________________________ Question 8. Table two is to include removal of equipment, shop supplies and testing removed equipment for factory operational status? Answer 8. Table two is for units deemed non reparable and would be scrapped. ________________________________________ Question 9. In the SOW (pages 86-92), it states that certain items need to be supplied but then, near the end of the document (pages 125-128) it states that those same items will be supplied by Ford. Currently, the items that state they are factory supplied, are coming factory supplied. I just want to check if they are coming from the factory, as normal, or if they will now be supplied by the contractor. The items in questions are as follows: "Four Wig-Wag strobe lights..." "Prisoner containment Equipment...." "Cargo barrier..." "Push Bumper" "Equipment Tray..." "Subframe with electronics sub panel..." Answer 9. Such equipment is already installed by Ford through Their own upfitter. ________________________________________ Question 10. I'm sure you were aware of this at the time but recently we had a truck arrive for transport that was deemed improper. Even though it came back a second time, and we loaded it, it was certainly not the proper vehicle and the MP units being loaded sustained slight damage during loading. This caused all kinds of issues between us, the DND, and the carrier. What recourse do we have in these situations and how do we ensure that DND property is protected and that we, as the contractor, are protected from any recourse or scrutiny when performing the loads for these? Answer 10. Contact the ILHQ. If they dispatch a commercial carrier that cannot accommodate the vehicle or meet the proper requirements for loading or handling the unit, refuse the delivery. Then, contact the ILHQ again and request that they arrange for a different commercial carrier. ________________________________________ Question 11. With reference to Annex A, Section 4.1.6, as well as the Mandatory Technical Criteria requiring the Contractor to have multiple regional locations, we noted that the response to Vendor Question 4 indicates that, from a logistical perspective, it would be preferable to have a facility in each province. Could DND please clarify whether having multiple regional facilities is a mandatory requirement for bid compliance? Answer 11. It is mandatory, you will need to have a facility in all 3 regions ________________________________________ Question 12. More specifically, would a supplier operating a single vehicle outfitting facility located in Quebec be eligible to submit a compliant bid for the entire requirement, including Western, Central and Eastern Canada, if all outfitting work is performed at this single facility? Answer 12. Para 4.1.6 of the SOW states -The repair and overhaul contract must have regionalized facilities to provide the above services in the following areas: a. Western Canada – BC to Manitoba; b. Central Canada – Ontario and Quebec; and c. c. Eastern Canada – New Brunswick to Newfoundland ________________________________________ Question 13. Under this approach, the vehicles would be transported to the supplier’s Quebec facility for outfitting and, once completed, transported to their required final destinations. description: L’Agence nationale des techniques d'enquêtes numériques judiciaires (ANTENJ) pilote les outils régaliens mis en œuvre en matière d’interceptions de communications électroniques et autres techniques numériques d’enquête. À ce titre, elle met à disposition des magistrats et enquêteurs plusieurs outils informatiques composant le Système d’information des techniques d’enquêtes numériques judiciaires (SITENJ). Dans ce cadre, la présente procédure a pour objet la mise à disposition, par un éditeur de solution standard du marché, d'une solution permettant de surveiller activement l’utilisation illicite éventuelle dans l’espace numérique de données issues du SITENJ qui, en grande majorité, sont strictement soumises au secret de l’enquête ou de l’instruction. Le détail des prestations et fonctionnalités figure dans le dossier de consultation mais la solution doit a minima offrir un service de : 1) veille permanente et de remontée d’information à destination des utilisateurs de l’administration (détection automatisée et alerte) ; 2) recherche active sur demande desdits utilisateurs (détection sur la base des éléments transmis).

title: Ireland – Building installation work – Fire Remediation Works at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan
description: The project involves the execution of fire remediation works to an existing 24-unit residential development located at Rowantree Court, Mullaghmonaghan, Monaghan, on behalf of the client, Oaklee Housing. The objective of the works is to address identified fire safety deficiencies in order to bring the building into compliance with current fire protection and life safety standards outlined in TGD Part B (Fire Safety) of the Building Regulations and other relevant codes such as IS 3218:2913 for fire alarm systems. The scope of the remediation works includes, but is not limited to: • Installation of fire-stopping systems at service penetrations and wall/floor junctions. • Replacement or upgrade of fire-rated doors, closers, and seals to comply with TGD-B. • Retrofitting of cavity barriers at floor levels in external cavity. • Fire alarm cable rerouting and improvements to service risers and shafts. • Sealing of socket/switch boxes within fire-rated partitions. • General improvement of compartmentation and passive fire protection measures. All works will be undertaken within a live residential environment, requiring a high level of coordination to minimise disruption to residents.

title: Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the following technical area: physics and nonlinear control of inertial measurement units (IMUs) appropriate for tactical and unmanned missions. The Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT) program will challenge the research community to overcome the decade-long performance plateau of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) IMUs by exploring revolutionary sensor architectures that operate in highly nonlinear regimes. DARPA is soliciting proposals for the research and development of novel inertial sensors based on physics such as, but not limited to, electromagnetically levitated proof masses, non-linear resonators, and high-velocity tethered microsystems. A central theme of this program is the tight co-design of the physical sensor package with advanced, real-time adaptive control systems necessary to stabilize and harness these complex dynamics. Performers should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.
